extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry / readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea'
extracted.subtask_description: Exercises, propositions, and remarks about properties and computation of Ext groups, the local-to-global spectral sequence, Yoneda cup product, the π!_sh construction, and Serre duality (including the adjunction formula for dualizing sheaves) on ringed spaces and projective k-schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom(·,I) exact for injective I
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose I is an injective O_X-module. Show that Hom_OX(·, I) is an exact contravariant functor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.2.A: use the definition of injectivity (cf. Exercise 23.2.C(a)). This fact is used repeatedly to obtain short exact sequences of Hom-complexes when taking an injective resolution of a module and applying Hom(·,I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction compatibility for Ext
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a ringed space, F and G are O_X-modules, and U is an open subset, then there is a canonical isomorphism Ext^i_X(F,G)|_U ≅ Ext^i_U(F|_U, G|_U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.2.B: take an injective resolution of G on X and restrict it to U; use Exercise 30.2.A to see the restriction is an injective resolution on U.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ext^i(O_X,G) and cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ringed space X and O_X-module G, Ext^i(O_X, G) = G if i=0 and 0 otherwise; moreover Ext^i(O_X,G) ≅ H^i(X,G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.2.C(a,b): compute Ext using an injective resolution of G; the identification with H^i(X,G) is the usual interpretation of global Ext against the structure sheaf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally free sheaf acyclicity for Ext
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is a locally free sheaf on X, then Ext^i(E, G) = 0 for i>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.2.D: follows from 30.2.C(a) and the fact that locally free sheaves are locally sums of O_X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute Ext via a locally free resolution of the first argument
rubrics_metrics.description: If ... → E1 → E0 → F → 0 is a resolution of an O_X-module F by locally free sheaves, then Ext^i(F,G) ≅ H^i(Hom(E•,G)). In other words, Ext(F,G) can be computed by taking a locally free resolution of F, applying Hom(·,G), and taking homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important Exercise 30.2.E: choose an injective resolution of G and consider the spectral sequence with E0-term Hom(E_p, I_q). Use affine-local arguments and free resolutions on affines to reduce computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence of Ext sheaves for coherent inputs
rubrics_metrics.description: If F and G are coherent sheaves on a quasiprojective k-scheme X, then Ext^i_X(F,G) is a coherent sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.2.F: argument works on any scheme where finite-rank locally free resolutions exist on coherent sheaves (reduce affine-by-affine and use algebraic coherence facts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence in Ext from short exact sequence of first arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0 → F' → F → F'' → 0 exact sequence of O_X-modules, there is a natural long exact sequence ... → Hom(F'',G) → Hom(F,G) → Hom(F',G) → Ext^1(F'',G) → Ext^1(F,G) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.2.G: take an injective resolution of G, apply Hom(·, I•) to the short exact sequence, and compute the long exact sequence in cohomology; use exactness of Hom(·,I) for injective I (Exercise 23.2.C(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor/Hom compatibility with locally free sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is a locally free sheaf on X, there are canonical isomorphisms Ext^i(F ⊗ E∨, G) ≅ Ext^i(F, G ⊗ E) and Ext^i(F ⊗ E, G) ≅ Ext^i(F, G) ⊗ E∨.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.2.H: show that if I is injective then I ⊗ E is injective (or use adjunction); these isomorphisms follow from Hom-tensor adjunction and properties of locally free sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injective → Hom(F,I) flasque (Γ-acyclic)
rubrics_metrics.description: If I is an injective O_X-module, then Hom(F,I) is flasque (hence Γ-acyclic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.2.J: prove surjectivity of restriction maps Hom(F,I)(V) → Hom(F,I)(U) for open inclusions j:U→V by noting I|_V is injective on V (Exercise 23.5.A) and applying Hom_V(·, I|_V) to the inclusion j_!(F|_U) → F|_V.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-to-global spectral sequence for Ext
rubrics_metrics.description: For ringed space X and O_X-modules F,G there is a spectral sequence with E2-term H^j(X, Ext^i(F,G)) abutting to Ext^{i+j}(F,G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.2.K: apply Grothendieck's composition-of-functors spectral sequence (Theorem 23.3.5); use acyclicity of Hom(F,I) for Γ (Exercise 30.2.J).

rubrics_metrics.name: Yoneda cup product / composition of Ext classes
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a graded associative composition (cup product) Ext^•(A,B) × Ext^•(B,C) → Ext^•(A,C) induced by composition of maps between resolutions; H•(A,A) is a graded ring and H•(A,B) a module over it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 30.2.3: define Hom•(A•,B•) as graded homomorphisms of complexes with differential δ(u)=du + (−1)^{n+1} u d, take cohomology to get Ext, and check independence of injective resolutions. See references [Gr3],[Cart].

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural pairing Hi(X,F) × Ext^j(F,G) → H^{i+j}(X,G)
rubrics_metrics.description: In particular (using Exercise 30.2.C(b)), there is a natural map Hi(X,F) × Ext^j(F,G) → H^{i+j}(X,G) coming from composition / Yoneda product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pairing underlies trace maps and the trace version of Serre duality for Ext (see end of §30.1 and later use in adjunctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of π!_sh as right adjoint to π_* for affine morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For an affine morphism (or for B→A rings) there is a construction π!_sh(G):=π^{-1} Hom_Y(π_* O_X, G) (sheafified) which yields a covariant functor QCoh_Y → QCoh_X and is right adjoint to π_* (on quasi-coherent sheaves).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 30.3.1–30.3.3 and Exercise 30.3.A: check the ring-theoretic adjunction Hom_A(M, Hom_B(A,N)) ≅ Hom_B(M_B, N) and sheafify; Exercise 30.3.B addresses globalizing and adjointness on QCoh categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction isomorphism Hom_X(F, π!_sh G) ≅ Hom_Y(π_* F, G)
rubrics_metrics.description: If F∈QCoh_X and G∈QCoh_Y, then Hom_X(F, π!_sh G) ≅ Hom_Y(π_* F, G) (this is the affine-local incarnation of the adjunction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equation (30.3.3.1): verify affine-locally via the ring-module bijection (30.3.2.1) from Exercise 30.3.A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of π!_sh for closed embeddings and injectives
rubrics_metrics.description: When π is a closed embedding, π!_sh(G):=Hom_Y(π_* O_X, G) naturally has O_X-module structure; π!_sh is right adjoint to π_* between module categories and sends injective O_Y-modules to injective O_X-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.3.C: construct the O_X-module structure (localize to open subsets) and use adjointness to check exactness/preservation of injectives (see Exercise 23.5.B hint).

rubrics_metrics.name: π!_sh agrees with Grothendieck π! in finite flat/derived contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: If π is finite and flat (or in the finite morphism locally Noetherian case), π!_sh coincides (in the appropriate sense) with Grothendieck's π! (one of the six operations) and defines adjoint pairs between Coh_X and Coh_Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks 30.3.2 and 30.3.4: check coherence and finiteness locally (Exercise 17.1.E and Exercise 14.3.A(b)); Miracle Flatness and finiteness results (e.g., Corollary 18.1.5) are used to relate projective affine morphisms to finiteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective scheme as finite cover of P^n
rubrics_metrics.description: Any projective k-scheme X of pure dimension n can be expressed as a finite morphism π: X → P^n (and if X is Cohen-Macaulay, π can be taken flat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 30.3.6 and Remark 30.3.7: construct by projecting from a linear space disjoint from X (use Veronese embedding when k finite); use Cancellation Theorem and properties of projective/affine morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport of Serre duality for vector bundles via π!_sh (flat case)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is finite and flat and functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for Y with dualizing sheaf ω_Y, then functorial Serre duality for vector bundles holds for X with dualizing sheaf π!_sh(ω_Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 30.3.9: proof uses adjointness, afﬁneness of π, projection formula, and functorial Serre duality on Y; flatness is used to ensure π_* F is locally free when F is.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport of Serre duality for Hom via trace (no flatness needed)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is finite and the trace version of Serre duality for Hom holds for Y with dualizing sheaf (ω_Y,t_Y), then functorial Serre duality for Hom holds for X with dualizing sheaf π!_sh ω_Y (trace for X comes from diagram (30.3.11.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 30.3.11: use adjointness of (π_*, π!_sh) and afﬁneness to commute the relevant Hom and cohomology maps; no flatness hypothesis is required here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functorial Serre duality for Ext on Cohen–Macaulay projective schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Functorial Serre duality for Ext holds for all equidimensional Cohen–Macaulay projective k-schemes (with an explicit dualizing sheaf constructed via finite covers of P^n and π!_sh).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollaries 30.3.10 and 30.3.14 together with Propositions 30.3.9 and 30.3.13: reduce to projective space case and use finite flat covers + projection formula + Serre vanishing to check δ-functor universality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing of lower Exts for closed embeddings (support/codimension criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose π: X → Y is a closed embedding of equidimensional projective k-schemes with codimension r. Then Ext^i_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y) = 0 for all i < r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 30.4.4: use coherence of Ext sheaves (Exercise 30.2.F), Serre vanishing, and local-to-global spectral sequence (Exercise 30.2.K) together with dimensional cohomology vanishing (Theorem 18.2.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of dualizing sheaf for closed embedding (adjunction formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is a closed embedding of equidimensional projective k-schemes with codimension r and Y satisfies functorial Serre duality for Ext, then ω_X = π^{-1} Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 30.4.3: proven by constructing π!_sh-applied injective resolutions, showing exactness up to index r (Lemma 30.4.5 and Exercises 30.4.B–E), and combining with functorial Serre duality on Y to identify Hom_X(·, π^{-1} Ext^r(π_* O_X, ω_Y)) ≅ H^n(X,·)^∨.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction for effective Cartier divisors: ω_X = ω_Y(X)|_X
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is Cohen–Macaulay projective of pure dimension n and X is an effective Cartier divisor on Y, then ω_X = ω_Y(X)|_X (hence invertibility of ω_Y implies invertibility of ω_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 30.4.8: compute Ext^1(π_* O_X, ω_Y) using the short exact closed subscheme sequence 0 → O_Y(−X) → O_Y → π_* O_X → 0 and apply the preceding identification ω_X = π^{-1} Ext^1(π_* O_X, ω_Y); tensoring and taking cokernels yields ω_X = ω_Y(X)|_X.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular embedding formula for Ext and dualizing sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: If X→Y is a codimension r regular embedding with normal sheaf N_{X/Y} locally free, then Ext^i_Y(π_* O_X, L) = 0 for i≠r and π^{-1} Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, L) ≅ (det N_{X/Y}) ⊗ L|_X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.4.G: this is a local statement (no projectivity needed); apply locally free resolutions / Koszul-type computations. Use this to deduce adjunction formula in regular embedding cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dualizing sheaf for complete intersections in P^n and identification with canonical bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a complete intersection in P^n of hypersurfaces of degrees d1,...,dr (hence Cohen–Macaulay), then ω_X ≅ det Ω_X and if X is smooth then ω_X ≅ K_X; concretely for a smooth complete intersection ω_X ≅ O_X(−n−1 + Σ d_i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 30.4.F and 30.4.I: use adjunction repeatedly and Exercise 21.5.B for adjunction of Ω; combine with earlier adjunction formula for Cartier divisors and the regular-embedding formula for det N_{X/P^n}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: compute Ext by applying π!_sh to injective resolutions of ω_Y
rubrics_metrics.description: To identify π^{-1} Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y) and related cohomology, choose an injective resolution 0 → ω_Y → I^0 → I^1 → ... of ω_Y, apply Hom_Y(π_*·, I^•) (or via adjointness apply π!_sh to I^•), and analyze the resulting complex whose cohomology computes the Ext sheaves; exactness up to degree r is key (Lemma 30.4.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 30.4.5 and Exercises 30.4.B–E: show π!_sh I^i are injective O_X-modules, analyze cohomology of the complex 0 → π!_sh I^0 → π!_sh I^1 → ... and split off summands to identify the r-th cohomology as π^{-1} Ext^r_Y(π_* O_X, ω_Y).
